title: A deformation of one affine open extends across a smooth affine open
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism of finite-dimensional commutative $k$-algebras, each augmented to $k$ with augmentation kernel its unique maximal ideal, respecting the augmentations. Let $X$ be a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] with an affine open covering $X=U\cup V$ such that $U\cap V$ is affine and both $U$ and $U\cap V$ are smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] with a specified special-fibre isomorphism $Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}k\cong X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For an open $W\subseteq X$, let $Y_W$ be the open subscheme corresponding to $W$ under the homeomorphism of underlying spaces of this nilpotent special fibre. Suppose a flat $A'$-scheme $Z$ and an $A$-isomorphism $e:Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A'}\operatorname{Spec}A\cong Y_V$ are given. Then there are a flat $A'$-scheme $Y'$, an $A$-isomorphism $\alpha:Y'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A'}\operatorname{Spec}A\cong Y$, and an $A'$-isomorphism $\gamma:Y'_V\cong Z$ such that $e\circ\gamma_A=\alpha|_{Y_V}$. Here $Y'_V$ is the corresponding open under the special-fibre identification induced by $\alpha$, and $\gamma_A$ denotes reduction to $A$. Empty opens are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0DZN, lemma-glueing-smooth, second assertion specialized to U_1 smooth (hence a local complete intersection); Situation situation-glueing, and Example example-schemes. The commutative reduction equation is the lifting condition in the definition of smooth morphism of deformation categories.

proof.text: Write $W=U\cap V$ and $J=\ker(A\to k)$, $J^\prime=\ker(A^\prime\to k)$, $K=\ker(A^\prime\to A)$. A descending chain of ideals in either finite-dimensional $k$-algebra stabilizes because its dimensions stabilize, so both rings are Artinian local. Thus $J$ and $J^\prime$ are nilpotent by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent], and $K\subseteq J^\prime$ is nilpotent too. Locally a special fibre is the closed subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}(B/JB)$, so [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] identifies its underlying space with that of the original scheme. The same holds with $J^\prime$. Hence all opens indexed by $U,V,W$ in $Y$ and $Z$ exist uniquely. Restrictions of $Y$ and $Z$ to these opens are flat: their local rings and their structural local homomorphisms are unchanged, so the defining stalk condition [def-weil-flat-morphism] is unchanged.

source.place: Tag 0DZN, lemma-glueing-smooth, second assertion for a smooth U_1; constructive affine version of its proof; Situation situation-glueing; lemma-open

proof.text: For a $k$-scheme $T$, write $T_B=T\times_k\operatorname{Spec}B$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-smooth-trivialization-lift] with $R=A$, $I=J$, the quotient identified with $k$ by the augmentation $A/J\cong k$, $T=U$, $D=Y_U$, and with $\theta_0$ the specified special-fibre identification. It gives an $A$-isomorphism $a:Y_U\xrightarrow{\sim}U_A$ inducing that identification on the special fibre. Since it induces the identity on the labelled open $U$ of $X$, its restriction is an isomorphism $a_W:Y_W\xrightarrow{\sim}W_A$.

source.place: Tag 0DZN, lemma-glueing-smooth, second assertion for a smooth U_1; constructive affine version of its proof; smoothness of the affine U_1 supplies a trivial deformation

proof.text: Take $L=U_{A^\prime}$. The projection $L\to\operatorname{Spec}A^\prime$ is smooth by clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change], and flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The inclusion $W\subseteq U$ base changes to an open immersion $W_{A^\prime}\subseteq L$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Let $E=Z_W$, the open of $Z$ labelled by $W$ through the special-fibre identification induced by $e$. By the same open-base-change statement, $E_A$ is an open of $Z_A$. Its underlying open is the one labelled by $W$, since reduction modulo the nilpotent $K$ is a homeomorphism as in step 1; thus $e$ restricts to an isomorphism $E_A\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_W$. In particular $\beta_0=a_W\circ e|_{E_A}:E_A\xrightarrow{\sim}W_A$ is a specified $A$-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0DZN, lemma-glueing-smooth, second assertion for a smooth U_1; constructive affine version of its proof; lemma-glueing, the two open pieces

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-smooth-trivialization-lift] again, now with $R=A^\prime$, $I=K$, the quotient $R_0=A^\prime/K$ identified with $A$ by the given surjection, $T=W$, $D=E$, and $\theta_0=\beta_0$. Its hypotheses hold: $K$ is nilpotent, $W$ is smooth affine by assumption, and $E$ is flat by the restriction calculation in step 1. It gives $b:E\xrightarrow{\sim}W_{A^\prime}$ with $b_A=a_W\circ e|_{E_A}$. Set $\varphi=b^{-1}:W_{A^\prime}\xrightarrow{\sim}E$. The specified reduction, rather than just an arbitrary isomorphism of the two lifts, will ensure compatibility with $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0DZN, lemma-glueing-smooth, second assertion for a smooth U_1; constructive affine version of its proof; lifting the overlap identification

proof.text: Glue $L$ and $Z$ along their opens $W_{A^\prime}$ and $E$ using $\varphi$ and $\varphi^{-1}$, by [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes]. For two pieces the gluing identities are $\varphi^{-1}\varphi=\mathrm{id}$ and $\varphi\varphi^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$, so these data satisfy every cocycle identity, even when an open is empty. Obtain open immersions $\iota_L:L\to Y^\prime$ and $\iota_Z:Z\to Y^\prime$ covering $Y^\prime$, with intersection exactly their specified opens and $\iota_L|_{W_{A^\prime}}=\iota_Z\varphi$. Their structural maps to $\operatorname{Spec}A^\prime$ agree because $b$ is an $A^\prime$-isomorphism; they glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. This map $Y^\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}A^\prime$ is flat: at every point its local structural homomorphism is that in one of the flat open pieces $L,Z$, and [def-weil-flat-morphism] is a condition on precisely these local homomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0DYZ, lemma-glueing, proof constructing the quasi-inverse from two overlapping deformations

proof.text: After base change to $A$, the two open copies still form an open cover by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]; they cover since every point of a fibre product projects to one of the two original opens. On these pieces define maps to $Y$ by $a^{-1}:L_A=U_A\to Y_U\subseteq Y$ and $e:Z_A\to Y_V\subseteq Y$. They agree along the overlap: for $\varphi_A=b_A^{-1}$ the equality $b_A=a_W e|_{E_A}$ gives $e\varphi_A=a_W^{-1}$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives an $A$-map $\alpha:Y^\prime_A\to Y$. For the inverse, the chart maps are $\iota_{L,A}a:Y_U\to Y^\prime_A$ and $\iota_{Z,A}e^{-1}:Y_V\to Y^\prime_A$. On $Y_W$, the equality $b_A=a_W e$ gives $\varphi_A a_W=e^{-1}|_{Y_W}$; hence $\iota_{L,A}a_W=\iota_{Z,A}\varphi_A a_W=\iota_{Z,A}e^{-1}|_{Y_W}$ by the reduced gluing relation. They give a map $Y\to Y^\prime_A$. Its two composites with $\alpha$ restrict to identities on the respective open covers, and the uniqueness clause of the same cited node makes them identities globally. The glued maps are over $A$: composing either map with the structural morphism agrees with the corresponding structural morphism on both charts, hence globally by the same uniqueness clause. Hence $\alpha$ is an $A$-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0DYZ, lemma-glueing, proof; explicit verification of the special-fibre and reduction identifications

proof.text: By [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], reduction of $Y^\prime$ modulo the nilpotent $J^\prime$ is a homeomorphism, so each open of its special fibre specifies a unique open subscheme of $Y^\prime$. On the open copy $\iota_Z(Z)$, the special-fibre identification induced by $\alpha$ is the given identification of $Z_k$ with $V$, because $\alpha\iota_{Z,A}=e$. Hence $\iota_Z(Z)=Y^\prime_V$. Define $\gamma:Y^\prime_V\xrightarrow{\sim}Z$ as the inverse of this open-copy isomorphism. Restricting $\alpha\iota_{Z,A}=e$ and composing with $\gamma_A$ gives $e\circ\gamma_A=\alpha|_{Y_V}$. If $V$ or $W$ is empty the same formulas use the unique empty-scheme maps; if $U$ is empty the construction is simply $Z$.
